newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia is rudderless, Yeltsin should quit - Lebed.
newsitem.headline: Russia is rudderless, Yeltsin should quit - Lebed.

text.p: Former national security chief Alexander Lebed said on Thursday Boris Yeltsin's admission to hospital with the first signs of pneumonia had left Russia rudderless and that the president should resign.
"There's simply a power vacuum. There's no power in the country. It's rudderless," he told reporters gathered outside his flat in western Moscow.
Yeltsin, 65, who underwent multiple heart bypass surgery in November, was taken to the Central Clinical Hospital in Moscow on Wednesday evening.

"The president is badly ill. It's a difficult age, he's had a difficult operation, a not entirely health way of life for the past 40 years. It doesn't leave much hope," said Lebed, sacked by Yeltsin last October for overt presidential ambitions.

"The question of the president's departure over his health is on the agenda. The longer this rule of regent, the graver the consequences," Lebed added, referring to presidential chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais who he accuses of grabbing power.

"(Yeltsin) should offer his resignation. The president is in hospital, the prime minister is on holiday and people have not been paid and are not paid. No one has dealt with the economy or is dealing with the economy...Someone has to answer for that, someone has to rule," he said.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, who would step in temporarily under the constitution if Yeltsin is incapacitated, had been expected to leave for a short holiday near Moscow on Thursday.
There was no word from officials about whether he would make the trip following the announcement Yeltsin was in hospital.
Lebed would make a strong candidate in a future election after coming third in the first round of last year's presidential poll.
Yeltsin brought him into the Kremlin to help beat off a communist challenger in the runoff and Lebed gained popularity in the post by ending Moscow's 21-month conflict in Chechnya.
Since his dismissal, after a serious clash with other Kremlin officials, Lebed has started moves to form his own political group. The next presidential election is due in the year 2000.
